title: 2 Stocks I'm Buying While The Market Panics
creator: Daniel Pronk
summary: Pronk opens bearish - walking through Michael Burry's tweets (market in denial, a 2000-2008-style event within 6-9 months, AI circular financing as fraud) and Ray Dalio's warning of a crash within 3 years - then rebuts both, arguing real third-party AI demand exists (he concludes Nvidia's revenue is not fraud, though he questions its sustainability given the 19x forward P/E) and that rate fears are short-term, driven by the Iran conflict and oil prices. He closes optimistic with a Bruce Flatt/Howard Marks clip and names the two stocks where the majority of his capital is flowing. Brookfield Asset Management (BAM) - BUY: hit unjustifiably by rate fears despite accelerating fundamentals; investor-day guide of 15-20% annual earnings compounding for 5 years, 4.5% dividend yield growing ~15%/yr, ~21x forward P/E near public-market lows - "one of the most attractive stocks in terms of risk/reward in the entire market." Construction Partners (ROAD) - BUY: unjustified selloff after a good Q3 with guidance raised a third time this year, 80-85% of next year's revenue contractually locked, oil/asphalt cost pass-throughs protecting margins, a doubled business by 2030; trading around six-year lows on price-to-EBITDA. NVDA gets extended discussion but no call (UNCERTAIN); LULU, the Brookfield family names and the hyperscalers are passing mentions. Caption garbles: "road" for ROAD, "Ebeta"/"Ibata" for EBITDA, "Bruce Flatt" for Bruce Flatt, "Michael Bur" for Burry, "Ray Dallio" for Dalio.
